Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise Q&A addressing each of the items your security team requested. I’ve also attached our short handback playbook (redwood-vpc-data-handback-process.pdf) which maps artifacts to your checklist.

Q1 — Tenant/handback process (what we execute):
- Data model: For Private/VPC deployments Redwood runs a control plane in our tenancy but all customer data (objects, model request logs, KV caches) are stored in the customer's VPC/S3 (or on-prem object store) and are controlled by your IAM/KMS.
- Normal teardown: On customer request or contract end we execute a coordinated teardown that performs: 1) application quiesce, 2) final object inventory (manifest), 3) removal of transient cached data in our runtime (KV caches) with a signed deletion run, 4) revoke any short-lived service credentials, 5) request customer approval to trigger final object lifecycle deletion per your policies.
- Backup handling: Redwood does not retain customer backups outside your managed storage. If snapshots were created by the customer's environment during integration, the timeline for their deletion is governed by your lifecycle policy — we provide the manifest and operation timestamps to help you purge.

Q2 — Evidence and artifacts we provide:
- Object manifest CSV (path + object size + last-modified) captured immediately before the final delete run.
- Deletion operation log (time-stamped) showing API calls to your object store (we sign these with our service cert).
- KV cache flush report for the runtime nodes (node id, cache keys count, flush completion timestamp).
- KMS integration record: If you use a customer-managed KMS/HSM, we provide the HSM operation log lines we observed (we never hold your keys). If Redwood generated any ephemeral keys on your behalf, we include the key rotation/zeroization record.
- Signed attestation letter on Redwood letterhead confirming execution of the steps above and listing artifact checksums.

Q3 — Cross-region replication and geo-locking:
- We do support geo-locking at provisioning: replication is disabled by default for Geo-Bound deployments. If replication was enabled during a trial, we can provide explicit replication disablement and a replication-clean log (object copies removed) as part of teardown.

Q4 — Timeline expectations:
- Standard turnaround: 3–7 business days to produce manifest + deletion logs after a confirmed teardown window.
- Attestation: signed attestation issued within 24 hours of successful deletion confirmation.

Attachments: redwood-vpc-data-handback-process.pdf (handback playbook).

Next steps: If this matches what you need I can loop in our compliance teammate for a short review and provide a Draft attestation for your legal to pre-approve. Happy to set a 30-minute call early next week.

Best,

Marissa — quick answers inline:

- KV cache flush fields: we can provide node id, cache_type (prefix vs session), number_of_keys, bytes_freed, start_ts, end_ts, and a SHA256 digest of the keys list. That digest avoids sending raw keys but gives verifiable evidence. No runtime PII included.

- Manifest: we have a CSV template (path, size_bytes, etag, last_modified, delete_marker_flag). Use that. Aditya can scrub the Helios doc and replace with a generic example.

- KMS/HSM: If customer manages keys in their KMS we only provide the observed key operation logs (audit entries). For ephemeral keys we generate for ops we will include the key id and zeroization timestamp; we cannot provide raw key material (obviously).

I added a draft attestation paragraph below you can slot into a letter: 

"Redwood Inference confirms that on {date/time} the following actions were executed for tenant {tenant_id} in the customer-managed VPC: manifest capture, KV cache flush, revocation of service credentials, and initiation of configured object lifecycle deletion. Artifacts produced: manifest.csv, deletion_log.json, kv_flush_report.csv, kms_observed_ops.log. Redwood provides this attestation for customer records and does not retain copies of the deleted objects in Redwood-managed storage."

I can prep the artifacts if you give me the tenant id.

-karthik
